# PLAN — iteration 2

## Current state assessment

Iteration 1 is the verified best: it recovered timing feasibility with WNS 0.148 ns and WHS 0.182 ns, using 133 LUTs, 112 FFs, and 5 DSP48s. The objective is now strictly higher register-to-register setup slack at the same 6.667 ns period. The supplied evidence does not identify iteration 1’s routed critical path, so the benefit of a source change is uncertain; any candidate still must preserve the one-cycle behavior and pass every gate.

## Hypothesis

Writing each transposed-stage multiply-add as one signed expression may help Vivado map it into a DSP48E1 MAC and improve register-to-register slack by reducing logic outside the DSP.

## Instruction for generator

Keep the transposed state recurrence and its reset and update behavior unchanged. Replace the `p0`–`p7` product wires and separate `pN + sM` assignments with explicit signed multiply-add expressions in the corresponding clocked state assignments, preserving 32-bit modular results and the `// @latency 1` annotation. Retain the output register’s synchronous reset and update behavior; do not add registers or change cycle latency. Compare the routed result against iteration 1 and retain it only if all verification and timing gates pass and register-to-register setup slack strictly improves.
